title: The Life of Jesus
description: Walk through the life and teaching of Jesus Christ in the Gospels, from his birth to his resurrection and commission to his followers.
objectives: Read the main events of Jesus' life in the Gospels
Notice what Jesus taught and how people responded to him
Consider who Jesus says he is

sessions.title: The Word became flesh
sessions.intro: John opens his Gospel before Bethlehem — with the eternal Word who was with God and was God.

questions.text: What does John say about the Word in verses 1-5?
What does verse 14 say happened, and why is that remarkable after verses 1-3?
According to verses 11-13, how did people respond to him, and what is given to those who received him?

sessions.title: The birth of Jesus
sessions.intro: Luke places Jesus' birth in history — the reign of Caesar Augustus — and tells of shepherds who hear the news first.

questions.text: Why were Joseph and Mary in Bethlehem (verses 1-5)?
What do the angels announce to the shepherds in verses 10-14?
How do the shepherds and Mary respond in verses 15-20?

sessions.title: Baptism and temptation
sessions.intro: Before his public ministry begins, Jesus is baptised by John and tested in the wilderness.

questions.text: What does the voice from heaven say in Matthew 3:17?
How does Jesus answer each temptation in Matthew 4:1-11?
Jesus' answers come from Deuteronomy, from Israel's time in the wilderness. What connection might Matthew be drawing?

sessions.title: Calling the first disciples
sessions.intro: Jesus begins to proclaim the good news of God's kingdom, calls fishermen to follow him, and heals many.

questions.text: What message does Jesus proclaim in Mark 1:14-15?
What does Jesus ask Simon, Andrew, James and John to do, and how do they respond?
Why do you think Jesus leaves the crowds to pray and move on (verses 35-39)?

sessions.title: The Sermon on the Mount
sessions.intro: Jesus teaches his disciples about the blessed life in God's kingdom and their place in the world.

questions.text: Who does Jesus call 'blessed' in verses 3-10?
What do the pictures of salt and light (verses 13-16) say about the disciples' role?
Which of the beatitudes surprises you most, and why?

sessions.title: Who is this?
sessions.intro: Jesus calms a storm and sets free a man no one could restrain. Both events raise the question of who Jesus is.

questions.text: What question do the disciples ask at the end of Mark 4:41?
How is the man described before and after he meets Jesus in Mark 5?
What does Jesus tell the man to do in Mark 5:19, and what does he do?

sessions.title: Parables of the lost
sessions.intro: When religious leaders grumble that Jesus welcomes sinners, he tells three stories about something lost and found.

questions.text: Who is Jesus speaking to, and why does he tell these parables (verses 1-3)?
What do the three parables have in common?
How does the older brother respond in verses 25-32, and who might he represent in the setting of verses 1-2?

sessions.title: Peter's confession
sessions.intro: At Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asks his disciples who they say he is, and then begins to speak of his coming death.

questions.text: What answers do people give about Jesus, and what does Peter say (verses 13-16)?
What does Jesus begin to explain in verse 21, and how does Peter react?
What does Jesus say following him involves in verses 24-26?

sessions.title: Entering Jerusalem
sessions.intro: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a colt, the crowds praise him, and he weeps over the city.

questions.text: Read Zechariah 9:9. What would the crowds have understood from Jesus riding a colt into Jerusalem?
What do the disciples shout in verse 38?
Why does Jesus weep over Jerusalem (verses 41-44)?

sessions.title: The last supper and the garden
sessions.intro: Jesus shares the Passover meal with his disciples and then prays on the Mount of Olives.

questions.text: The meal is the Passover. What did the Passover remember, and how does Jesus give new meaning to the bread and cup?
What does Jesus pray in verse 42?
What does Jesus tell his disciples to pray for in verses 40 and 46?

sessions.title: The cross
sessions.intro: Jesus is crucified between two criminals. Luke records his words from the cross and the responses of those around him.

questions.text: What does Jesus say from the cross in verses 34, 43 and 46?
How do the different people around the cross respond to him?
What does the conversation with the second criminal (verses 39-43) show?

sessions.title: He is risen
sessions.intro: The women find the tomb empty; later Jesus appears to his disciples, opens the Scriptures to them and sends them out.

questions.text: What do the angels say to the women in verses 5-7?
How does Jesus show the disciples that he is really alive (verses 36-43)?
According to verses 44-49, what does Jesus say the Scriptures were pointing to, and what will his followers do?
